articles.title_zh: 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted
facts_zh:
'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted
- Published
"It flooded up to here in March," Agnes Shikoli says, pointing to a spot halfway up the six-foot [1.8m] corrugated iron wall of her home in Kibera, one of the largest informal settlements in Kenya.
Her tiny house lies just a couple of metres from the Ngong river, which runs through this densely populated area in the capital, Nairobi.
The scars of floods in the long rainy season earlier this year can still be seen - including a broken TV in the corner which was immersed in water.

all_titles.en: 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted

articles.title_zh: Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for rail crash victims
facts_zh:
Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for rail crash victims
- Published
Spain's King Felipe and Queen Letizia were among those who have attended a memorial service in tribute to the 69 victims of last month's deadly train crash.

The accident occurred when one train, travelling at high speed, ploughed into the back of another that was stationary on the Madrid-Seville line, near the small town of Urda, about 40 miles from Toledo.
It was the worst rail tragedy in Spain since 2013.

Nationwide protests by pro-Hasina activists started a day after the former leader said she had requested a passport to return to Bangladesh from exile in India.

articles.title_original: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
articles.title_zh: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
facts_zh:
Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
- Published
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) told makers of popular weight-loss GLP-1 drugs that they must add warning labels about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness.
Manufacturers of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and Zepbound must warn about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).
The disorder happens when vessels supplying blood to the optic nerves become blocked, depriving the nerves of oxygen.

Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
- Published
Malaysia's disgraced former Prime Minister Najib Razak has arrived home to begin serving the rest of a jail sentence for corruption under house arrest.
There was a big media presence at his Kuala Lumpur residence to see the 73-year-old return from prison in an SUV late on Tuesday night, escorted by a heavily armed police convoy.
Najib's return ended a four-year prison stint after he was found guilty over the embezzlement of billions of dollars from the country's sovereign wealth fund.

Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
- Published
Israel's new parliament has been sworn in, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The former army chief has been tasked with forming a government after receiving more recommendations from members of the Knesset than Netanyahu, although not all those backing him are willing to govern together.
Eisenkot's bloc of four parties won 48 seats in October's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
- Published
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has called on Israel to immediately allow all necessary humanitarian supplies into Gaza after rain flooded tens of thousands of tents.
The US-backed body, established to oversee the implementation of Trump's Gaza peace plan, acknowledged the steps now being considered by Israel, but said "the response remains insufficient".

Israel's military agency in charge of co-ordinating aid into Gaza said it had allowed in tens of thousands of tents and trucks with winter supplies, but added reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".

French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
- Published
One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104.
Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters.
After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir.

articles.title_original: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
articles.title_zh: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
facts_zh:
California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
- Published
Police in Santa Barbara, California, are investigating after nearly 30 people had to seek medical care at a half-marathon running event held in the city on Sunday.

In a statement provided to the BBC's US partner CBS News, officers said they received a report from Santa Barbara Cottage Hospital about race participants who sought medical treatment "for unusual symptoms" after the race ended.
"The cause of the reported symptoms has not been confirmed," the statement added.
